summary: AppContainer grant trees and killed-run reclaim at 4fa5f118f1, in bake-sandbox's Windows AppContainer runner, which Bake's default provider does not select: on Windows it still refuses with windows_acl::DEFAULT_REFUSAL. Before a grant that would propagate down a workspace or read root, the runner walks the root's tree under the per-path lock and refuses a reparse point, a file with more than one name, or an object owned by someone other than the token's user or default owner; each run writes a run record under %TEMP%\bake-appcontainer-runs so that the next run in its namespace reclaims the profile of a runner that has exited; and new Windows enforcement cases cover hard links, foreign-owned descendants, junctions, killed-runner reclaim, named objects, HKCU keys, objects created after resume, NUL with Git, and loopback. No Windows host was available, and GitHub CI runs Windows only on the develop to main release pull request, so no Windows case has run: every Windows result is missing, and Windows confinement stays unqualified and refused by default. The evidence is portable and compile-only. At HEAD 519a202b13, where bake-sandbox is byte-identical to the candidate, the second full Linux preflight passed 33 gates (actionlint and runtime skipped) after a first attempt under umask 077 failed two packaging gates on an archive mode check, and the Intel x86_64 macOS native preflight passed 4 gates; each rust gate passed the five new windows_appcontainer unit tests, which test pure helpers, and cross-target Clippy at HEAD compiled and linted the Windows runner and cases for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu clean. The slice's saved workspace test log passed the same unit tests; its saved whole-workspace cross-target Clippy log exits 1 on another slice's bake-cli test dead code. The loopback owner decision, Git's NUL blocker, profile registry storage under read-only, brokered objects after resume, and Apple Silicon remain. Before push the stack was rebased onto develop c5f02c476a (scope 12 web tools and hooks, scope 15 commands), which changed every hash: this record's candidate 4fa5f118f1 became ec58dc9375 and its base b813395413 became d8bc9a097e, with the fixture bytes unchanged. The runs above at 519a202b13 are pre-rebase. A second run set at bfdbbcb875, the rebased stack with three integration commits on top (Windows lint fixes in the scope 12 and 15 code, D41's inconclusive loopback timeout, and Never replay classes for web_search and web_fetch), passed: the Linux preflight's 33 gates (actionlint and the TypeScript runtime skipped; 2534 Cargo tests, 6 ignored; PTY 58/58), the Intel macOS native preflight's 4 gates (2512, 6 ignored; PTY 56/56), and cross-target Clippy for Windows and Apple Silicon.

results.behavior: The five new windows_appcontainer unit tests passed in the Linux and Intel macOS rust gates at HEAD and in the slice's workspace test log. a_propagating_grant_refuses_links_reparse_points_and_foreign_owners: a file with one name and a directory with link count 7 pass; a reparse point is refused first whatever its link count or owner, then a file with two names, then a foreign owner. a_run_reclaims_only_records_of_its_own_namespace: untagged runs, a tagged run, and another tag never reclaim each other's records, and truncated, overlong, upper-case, path-like, and .tmp-suffixed names are never reclaimable. run_records_round_trip_and_refuse_partial_text: pid 4242 created 133000000000000000 and the u32 and u64 maxima round-trip, and a record without its newline, with a doubled space, a sign, an extra field, an overflowing value, an upper-case key, or CRLF names no runner. only_a_failed_deletion_keeps_a_reclaimed_record: S_OK, S_FALSE, and the not-found HRESULTs release the record; access denied, a sharing violation, and E_FAIL keep it. a_grant_root_may_not_contain_the_run_records: a workspace or read root that is or holds the record directory is refused; a sibling under the same temporary directory is not. They test pure helpers over the host's path syntax and make no Win32 call, so they decide nothing about Windows enforcement. Counts describe Cargo tests, summed per test binary.

In the rust gates at HEAD, bake-sandbox's library tests and enforcement harness passed: on Linux 88 library tests and 32 enforcement cases, on Intel macOS 85 and 11. Each library run included 20 windows_appcontainer::tests, the five new ones among them. The enforcement cases that ran are the Linux and macOS backends' own; the Windows enforcement files compile only for Windows. This shows the candidate's crate changes left the Linux and macOS backends' tests passing. Counts describe Cargo tests and enforcement cases.

Cross-target Clippy at HEAD ran over the whole workspace, all targets, with -D warnings, for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and aarch64-apple-darwin. In both passes it re-checked bake-sandbox, with bake-coding-agent, bake-tui, and bake-cli, the other crates being fresh, and it ended exit 0 with no warning or error, so the AppContainer runner, the grant walk, the run records, and the Windows enforcement cases in windows_appcontainer.rs and windows_appcontainer_objects.rs compile and lint for Windows. missingEvidence.what: The native AppContainer enforcement suite, every new and changed case included
missingEvidence.reason: No Windows host was available, and GitHub CI runs Windows only on the develop to main release pull request, so every case is compile-checked only. F's report expects that a first native run may fail for test-side reasons: whether Session\<n>\<name> resolves the user's Local\ objects from both sides, the form FileNameInfo reports for a container's LOCAL\ pipe, whether GetAppContainerNamedObjectPath's prefix opens as a Win32 name from outside, and whether HKCU's ACL denies a container with code 5.

Git for Windows opens /dev/null (NUL) for reading and writing at every start, and in CI 39033317835 git --version failed on it, per the module documentation. F's report adds no runner defense, because making NUL openable would change the null device's security for the whole host, which D24 does not authorize; the test only checks that Git follows the measured NUL verdict. Git stays a qualification blocker.

The read-only pass covers only the filesystem; named_objects_and_the_registry_stay_closed records, without asserting, whether a container can create keys in its profile's registry storage. If it can under read-only, that is a blocker; the storage is deleted with the profile.

An object a system broker creates under the profile after resume, with its own explicit ACEs, is covered by neither read-only pass, and no test covers it; objects_made_after_resume_end_with_the_run covers only objects the command makes itself.

missingEvidence.what: The foreign-owner refusal on an elevated host
missingEvidence.reason: foreign_owned_descendants_refuse_a_propagating_grant needs SeRestorePrivilege to set a SYSTEM owner; a native run without it prints appcontainer-unproven and proves nothing.

The walk is a check, not a lock: an object the user's own unconfined process swaps in between the walk and the propagation is not seen. It refuses common trees: rustup's hard-linked proxies, a pnpm store and its linked node_modules, a local git clone's hard-linked objects, symbolic links and junctions, OneDrive placeholders, and objects owned by SYSTEM or TrustedInstaller. A file linked into a granted tree after its first grant keeps its own DACL, so the container cannot use it. A tree with more than MAX_GRANT_OBJECTS (1 << 20) objects is refused. Each grant root keeps its propagated ACEs, and nothing removes them. These come from the code and its documentation; none was observed natively.

Reclaim needs a later run in the same namespace and the same %TEMP%; a runner killed before writing its record, or a profile from a runner without records, is never reclaimed. Each run scans at most 1024 records and reclaims at most 8, and a failure prints a cleanup: line without failing the run. F's report notes that a process running as the user outside the container could forge a record for a moniker no runner holds, and the worst effect is deleting that profile.

The shared Job's account passed natively for the restricted-token runner; this runner's use of it, including the suspended-start failure paths, is unchanged by this candidate and has not run natively.
